district.description: Formerly a princely state, Pudukkottai is an archaeological treasure trove featuring Jain cave frescoes, early Chola structural temples, and megalithic burial sites.

culturalEntries.title: Thirumayam Fort and Cave Temples
culturalEntries.shortDescription: A massive 17th-century rock fort known for its association with the Polygar Wars, surrounded by two ancient rock-cut cave temples dedicated to Shiva and Vishnu.
culturalEntries.fullDescription: Constructed in 1687 CE by Sethupathi Vijaya Raghunatha Tevan of Ramanathapuram, the Thirumayam Fort is of immense historical importance. It is locally known as 'Oomayan Kottai' because Oomathurai, the deaf-mute brother of the legendary freedom fighter Veerapandiya Kattabomman, was captured here by the British. At the foot of the fort rock lie two stunning Pallava/Pandya era rock-cut cave temples (7th-8th century): the Satyagirisathar (Shiva) temple and the Sathyamurthi Perumal (Vishnu) temple, showcasing remarkable early Dravidian rock-cut architecture.
culturalEntries.historyOrigin: Cave temples carved in the 7th/8th centuries; Fort built in 1687 CE by Sethupathi kings.
culturalEntries.culturalSignificance: A unique site integrating early rock-cut religious shrines with late-medieval military fortifications. It symbolizes the fierce resistance of Tamil chieftains (Polygars) against British colonial rule.
culturalEntries.sourceReferences: State Archaeological and Historical Documentation; Tamil Nadu Tourism

chatbotKnowledge.answerEn: Thirumayam Fort in Pudukkottai is a 17th-century stronghold associated with freedom fighter Oomathurai. It sits atop a hill that houses two ancient 8th-century rock-cut cave temples dedicated to Lord Shiva and Lord Vishnu.
chatbotKnowledge.answerTa: புதுக்கோட்டையில் உள்ள திருமயம் கோட்டை 17-ஆம் நூற்றாண்டில் கட்டப்பட்டது. இது சுதந்திரப் போராட்ட வீரர் ஊமைத்துரையுடன் தொடர்புடையது. இக்கோட்டை அமைந்துள்ள மலையின் அடிவாரத்தில் 8-ஆம் நூற்றாண்டைச் சேர்ந்த பழமையான சிவன் மற்றும் விஷ்ணு குடைவரைக் கோயில்கள் உள்ளன.
